Suppose we have a singular value decomposition $A = U\Sigma V^T$ where $$ U = \begin{bmatrix} \uvec_1 \amp \uvec_2 \amp \uvec_3 \amp \uvec_4 \end{bmatrix},\hspace{24pt} \Sigma = \begin{bmatrix} 18 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 4 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{bmatrix},\hspace{24pt} V = \begin{bmatrix} \vvec_1 \amp \vvec_2 \amp \vvec_3 \end{bmatrix}\text{.} $$

What is the shape of $A$? What is $\rank(A)$?

Identify bases for $\col(A)$ and $\col(A^T)$.

Explain why $$ U\Sigma = \begin{bmatrix} \uvec_1 \amp \uvec_2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 18 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 4 \amp 0 \\ \end{bmatrix}\text{.} $$

Explain why $$ \begin{bmatrix} 18 \amp 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 4 \amp 0 \\ \end{bmatrix}V^T = \begin{bmatrix} 18 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 4 \\ \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} \vvec_1 \amp \vvec_2 \end{bmatrix}^T\text{.} $$

If $A = U\Sigma V^T$, explain why $A=U_r\Sigma_rV_r^T$ where the columns of $U_r$ are an orthonormal basis for $\col(A)$, $\Sigma_r$ is a square, diagonal, invertible matrix, and the columns of $V_r$ form an orthonormal basis for $\col(A^T)$.
